recipes.title: Korean beef rice bowl, light
recipes.summary: A lean but satisfying Korean-style bowl with savoury beef, fluffy rice and plenty of fresh vegetables. Lime and sesame seeds keep it bright and punchy.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear so the grains cook up fluffy rather than sticky.
Cook the rice in lightly salted water until tender, then cover and let it stand off the heat for a minute so the rice finishes steaming.
Slice the onion finely and chop the garlic and ginger so everything is ready to go into the pan quickly.
Heat the sesame oil in a wide pan and cook the onion until soft and translucent, stirring now and then so the onion sweetens without catching.
Add the ground beef, garlic, ginger and soy sauce, then cook until the beef is browned and the sauce turns glossy and clings to the meat.
Cut the carrot and cucumber into neat thin pieces so they stay crisp and fresh in the finished bowl.
Fold the spinach into the hot beef mixture and stir just until the spinach wilts down and turns bright green.
Spoon the rice into a bowl and top with the beef, carrot, cucumber and spinach, then finish with a squeeze of lime and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

recipes.storageNotes: Best assembled fresh for the crispest cucumber, but the cooked rice and beef keep well. Refrigerate up to 3 days and reheat the rice and beef before adding fresh cucumber, lime and sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Korean beef rice bowl
recipes.summary: A balanced Korean-style rice bowl with savoury beef, tender spinach and crunchy vegetables. It is quick to cook and feels fresh as well as hearty.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear so the grains stay separate after cooking.
Cook the rice in lightly salted water until tender, then cover it briefly off the heat so the rice finishes steaming and fluffs up.
Slice the onion finely and chop the garlic and ginger so the aromatics are ready before you start frying.
Heat the sesame oil in a wide pan and cook the onion until soft and translucent, stirring a few times as it cooks.
Add the ground beef, garlic, ginger and soy sauce, then cook until the beef is fully browned and the sauce has reduced to a savoury glaze.
Cut the carrot and cucumber into thin strips or slices so they add crisp texture to the bowl.
Fold the spinach into the hot beef mixture and stir just until the spinach has wilted but still looks bright.
Spoon the rice into a bowl and top with the beef, carrot, cucumber and spinach, then finish with lime and sesame seeds.

recipes.storageNotes: The rice and beef mixture keep well for meal prep. Refrigerate up to 3 days and reheat before topping with fresh cucumber, lime and sesame seeds for the best texture.

recipes.title: Korean beef rice bowl, hearty
recipes.summary: A bigger Korean-style bowl with extra beef and rice for a training day or a hungry evening. The fresh vegetables and lime stop it from feeling heavy.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water looks mostly clear so the rice cooks evenly and does not turn gluey.
Cook the rice in lightly salted water until tender, then let the rice stand covered for a minute to finish steaming.
Slice the onion finely and chop the garlic and ginger so the aromatics are ready for the pan.
Heat the sesame oil in a wide pan and cook the onion until soft and translucent, stirring now and then.
Add the ground beef, garlic, ginger and soy sauce, then cook until the beef is well browned and the sauce has reduced to a glossy coating.
Cut the carrot and cucumber into thin strips or slices so they stay crisp and easy to eat.
Fold the spinach into the hot beef mixture and stir until the spinach has just wilted into the pan.
Spoon the rice into a bowl and top with the beef, carrot, cucumber and spinach, then finish with lime and sesame seeds.

recipes.storageNotes: Good for meal prep. Refrigerate the cooked rice and beef for up to 3 days, or freeze in portions. Add the cucumber, lime and sesame seeds after reheating so the bowl stays fresh.

recipes.title: Caribbean coconut shrimp rice, light
recipes.summary: Tender shrimp and fragrant rice cooked with coconut milk, brightened with lime and cilantro. This lighter version keeps the tropical feel while leaning on extra vegetables.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear so the cooked rice stays fluffy.
Cook the rice with the coconut milk and vegetable broth until tender, then let the rice stand covered for a minute so it finishes steaming.
Chop the onion and bell pepper, and prepare the garlic and ginger so the aromatics are ready to go into the pan.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pan and cook the onion and bell pepper until they soften and smell sweet.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin and paprika, then stir for a moment until the pan smells warm and fragrant.
Add the shrimp and cook just until the shrimp turn pink and opaque all the way through.
Stir in the cilantro and squeeze in the lime so the shrimp mixture tastes bright and fresh.
Serve the shrimp mixture over the rice, making sure each bowl gets plenty of pepper and a little extra lime on the side.

recipes.storageNotes: Best fresh because shrimp can toughen on reheating, though leftovers are still good. Refrigerate up to 2 days. Freeze only the rice base if needed, as the shrimp are best not frozen after cooking.

recipes.title: Caribbean coconut shrimp rice
recipes.summary: A quick Caribbean-inspired plate of shrimp, coconut rice and sweet pepper with lime and cilantro. It is fragrant, colourful and easy to cook on a weeknight.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear so the grains stay separate.
Cook the rice with the coconut milk and vegetable broth until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender, then let it stand covered briefly.
Chop the onion and bell pepper, and prepare the garlic and ginger so everything is ready before frying.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pan and cook the onion and bell pepper until soft and lightly sweet.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin and paprika, then stir for a moment to bloom the spices without letting them burn.
Add the shrimp and cook until the shrimp are pink, plump and opaque from edge to centre.
Stir in the cilantro and squeeze in the lime so the whole pan tastes fresh and balanced.
Serve the shrimp mixture over the rice, making sure the pepper and fragrant juices are spooned over the top.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat gently so the shrimp stay tender. The cooked rice freezes better than the finished shrimp mixture, which is nicest eaten fresh.

recipes.title: Caribbean coconut shrimp rice, hearty
recipes.summary: A fuller Caribbean-inspired meal with extra shrimp, more rice and a richer touch of coconut milk. Lime and cilantro keep the flavours lively rather than heavy.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water looks mostly clear so the rice cooks up fluffy.
Cook the rice with the coconut milk and vegetable broth until tender and fragrant, then let the rice stand covered for a minute.
Chop the onion and bell pepper, and prepare the garlic and ginger so the pan work goes quickly.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pan and cook the onion and bell pepper until softened and lightly sweetened.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin and paprika, then stir until the spices smell toasty and warm.
Add the shrimp and cook until the shrimp are pink and opaque but still juicy.
Stir in the cilantro and squeeze in the lime so the rich coconut notes stay bright and fresh.
Serve the shrimp mixture over the rice, spooning the fragrant pan juices over the top with the pepper.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheats best over gentle heat. The rice can be frozen separately, but the shrimp are juiciest when the dish is eaten fresh.

recipes.title: Scandinavian salmon potato plate, light
recipes.summary: A fresh Scandinavian-style plate of salmon, potatoes and green beans with a cool dill yogurt sauce. The lighter version leans on extra vegetables while keeping the salmon generous.

steps.instruction: Cut the potato into bite-size pieces so it cooks quickly and evenly.
Simmer the potato in salted water until tender enough to pierce easily with a knife, then drain well.
Trim the green beans and slice the cucumber thinly so both are ready to finish the plate.
Stir the greek yogurt with the dill weed and lemon juice until smooth and cool, then set the sauce aside.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the salmon until the flesh is just opaque and flakes easily with gentle pressure.
Cook the green beans in boiling water until bright green and just tender, then drain them well.
Arrange the salmon with the potato, green beans and cucumber, then spoon over the yogurt sauce before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Best fresh, though leftovers keep well. Refrigerate up to 2 days. Keep the yogurt sauce separate if possible and add it after reheating the salmon, potato and beans. Not ideal for freezing.

recipes.title: Scandinavian salmon potato plate
recipes.summary: A simple Scandinavian-style plate with flaky salmon, tender potatoes, crisp cucumber and a cool dill yogurt sauce. It is clean, comforting and easy to put together.

steps.instruction: Cut the potato into bite-size pieces so they cook through at the same rate.
Simmer the potato in salted water until tender, then drain well and let the steam dry them slightly.
Trim the green beans and slice the cucumber thinly so the vegetables are ready to serve.
Stir the greek yogurt with the dill weed and lemon juice until smooth and spoonable.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the salmon until lightly golden outside and just cooked in the centre.
Cook the green beans in boiling water until bright and tender-crisp, then drain them.
Arrange the salmon with the potato, green beans and cucumber, then spoon the yogurt sauce over the plate.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days. The yogurt sauce is best kept separate and stirred before serving again. The finished dish is not ideal for freezing, but the cooked salmon and potato can be frozen if needed.

recipes.title: Scandinavian salmon potato plate, hearty
recipes.summary: A heartier Scandinavian-style plate with extra salmon and potatoes, finished with crisp cucumber and dill yogurt. It feels filling without losing its clean, fresh character.

steps.instruction: Cut the potato into bite-size pieces so they cook through evenly and are easy to serve.
Simmer the potato in salted water until tender, then drain them well so they do not water down the plate.
Trim the green beans and slice the cucumber thinly so the vegetables are ready when the salmon finishes.
Stir the greek yogurt with the dill weed and lemon juice until smooth and well mixed.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the salmon until the outside is lightly coloured and the centre flakes easily.
Cook the green beans in boiling water until bright green and tender-crisp, then drain them well.
Arrange the salmon with the potato, green beans and cucumber, then spoon over the yogurt sauce and serve.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days. Store the yogurt sauce separately when you can, and reheat the salmon and potato gently. The complete plated dish is best fresh and is not ideal for freezing.

recipes.title: German potato and egg skillet, light
recipes.summary: A lighter German-style skillet of potatoes, eggs, mushrooms and spinach. Extra vegetables keep it generous while the eggs make it still feel like a proper meal.

steps.instruction: Dice the potato into small even pieces so they cook quickly in the skillet.
Simmer the potato in salted water until just tender, then drain well so the pieces can brown rather than steam.
Slice the onion and mushrooms so they are ready to go into the pan together.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the onion and mushrooms until the mushrooms lose their moisture and the onion softens.
Add the potato, spinach and paprika, then stir until the spinach wilts and the potato is coated in the warm spice.
Crack the eggs over the skillet and cook until the eggs are set to your liking, covering briefly if needed for a firmer top.
Serve the skillet hot, making sure each portion gets potato, mushrooms, spinach and eggs.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten fresh while the eggs are soft, though leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a pan. Not recommended for freezing because the eggs and potato lose texture.

recipes.title: German potato and egg skillet
recipes.summary: A comforting German-style skillet with browned potatoes, eggs, mushrooms and spinach. It works well for breakfast or lunch and comes together with simple pantry ingredients.

steps.instruction: Dice the potato into small even pieces so they cook evenly and fit neatly in the skillet.
Simmer the potato in salted water until almost tender, then drain well and let off some steam.
Slice the onion and mushrooms so they are ready to cook together.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the onion and mushrooms until the mushrooms are browned in spots and the onion is soft.
Add the potato, spinach and paprika, then stir until the spinach wilts and the potato is hot all the way through.
Crack the eggs over the skillet and cook until the eggs are set how you like them, covering the pan briefly if needed.
Serve the skillet hot so the potato stays crisp around the edges and the eggs stay tender.

recipes.storageNotes: Best fresh, but leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days and can be reheated in a skillet. The eggs will firm up on reheating. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: German potato and egg skillet, hearty
recipes.summary: A bigger German-style skillet with extra potatoes and an extra egg for a more filling start to the day. Mushrooms and spinach keep it savoury and balanced.

steps.instruction: Dice the potato into small even pieces so the larger amount still cooks quickly and evenly.
Simmer the potato in salted water until almost tender, then drain well so it can brown in the skillet.
Slice the onion and mushrooms so they are ready for the pan.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and cook the onion and mushrooms until softened and lightly browned.
Add the potato, spinach and paprika, then stir until the spinach wilts and the potato is coated and hot.
Crack the eggs over the skillet and cook until the eggs are set to your liking, using a lid briefly if you want the tops more firm.
Serve the skillet hot, making sure the potatoes, mushrooms, spinach and eggs are evenly divided.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served straight from the pan. Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat best in a skillet over low heat. The eggs and potato do not freeze well.

recipes.title: West African peanut chicken stew, light
recipes.summary: A lighter West African-inspired stew with tender chicken in a tomato and peanut butter sauce, served with rice. Extra spinach keeps it generous and satisfying.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water looks mostly clear so the rice cooks up fluffy.
Cook the rice in lightly salted water until tender, then keep it covered off the heat while you finish the stew.
Chop the onion and prepare the garlic and ginger so the base of the stew is ready for the pan.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pot and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, ginger and cumin, then stir for a moment until the aromatics smell warm and fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, chicken stock and peanut butter, then stir until the peanut butter has melted into a smooth sauce.
Add the chicken thigh pieces and simmer gently until the thigh is cooked through and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Stir in the spinach and cook just until the spinach wilts into the stew.
Serve the stew over the rice and finish with a squeeze of lime to brighten the sauce.

recipes.storageNotes: This stew reheats very well. Refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze in portions for up to 2 months. The rice can be stored separately so it stays fluffy.

recipes.title: West African peanut chicken stew
recipes.summary: A warming West African-inspired stew of chicken, tomatoes and peanut butter, served with rice. The sauce is rich and savoury, with spinach and lime to keep it lively.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water looks mostly clear so the grains stay separate.
Cook the rice in lightly salted water until tender, then keep the rice covered while you finish the stew.
Chop the onion and prepare the garlic and ginger so the aromatic base is ready to cook.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pot and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, ginger and cumin, then stir until fragrant without letting the aromatics colour too much.
Add the tomatoes, chicken stock and peanut butter, then stir until the peanut butter dissolves into a smooth, rich sauce.
Add the chicken thigh pieces and simmer gently until the thigh is tender and cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the spinach and cook just until the spinach has wilted into the sauce.
Serve the stew over the rice and squeeze over the lime just before eating.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps very well for meal prep. Refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat gently, adding a splash of water if the peanut butter sauce has thickened too much.

recipes.title: West African peanut chicken stew, hearty
recipes.summary: A bigger bowl of West African-inspired chicken stew with extra rice, more chicken and a richer peanut butter sauce. It is hearty enough for a hard training day or a very hungry evening.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water looks mostly clear so the rice cooks fluffy and separate.
Cook the rice in lightly salted water until tender, then keep the rice covered while you finish the stew.
Chop the onion and prepare the garlic and ginger so the stew base is ready to cook.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pot and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, ginger and cumin, then stir until the aromatics smell rich and warm.
Add the tomatoes, chicken stock and peanut butter, then stir until the peanut butter melts fully into the sauce.
Add the chicken thigh pieces and simmer gently until the thigh is cooked through and tender and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Stir in the spinach and cook until the spinach has just wilted into the stew.
Serve the stew over the rice and finish with lime for a fresh sharp contrast to the rich sauce.

recipes.storageNotes: Excellent for batch cooking. Refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze in portions for up to 2 months. Reheat gently and loosen the sauce with a splash of water if needed.
